items.q: What should you remember about **Names matter for agent workflows**?
items.a: **"spec" and "tickets" are renamed because precise** naming ("good friction") shapes what the LLM and user let leak into each document.

items.q: What should you remember about **Wayfinder = planning sharded across sessions**?
items.a: **each decision scoped to one agent session; blocking** sub-issue graph on GitHub replaces in-session handoff anxiety; Matt uses it "for literally everything," even planning his course.

items.q: What should you remember about **Ticket types classify the work**?
items.a: **research (AFK background agent), grilling (human-in-the-loop),** prototype (cheap concrete artifact), task (boring human config/provisioning that can't be automated).

items.q: What should you remember about **Implement earns its place by being trivial**?
items.a: **mostly leans on agent priors** and harness; exists because everyone kept asking "what's the flow?".

items.q: What should you remember about **Fowler smells as prior-invocation**?
items.a: **old, well-cited vocabulary is already deep in the model; one** sentence per smell makes the reviewer echo the term back ("found message chains, removing them"); "outrageously useful" for ~10 lines.

items.q: What should you remember about **Coding standards live outside AGENTS.md**?
items.a: **pushed to the reviewer** where they're most useful, not into every implementer session.

items.q: What should you remember about **Refactoring is review's job, not TDD's**?
items.a: **red-green only, one slice at** a time; putting refactoring in code review avoids overloading implementation.

items.q: What should you remember about **Grilling fixes**?
items.a: **tell the model *why* multiple questions are bewildering; add "do not** enact until I confirm shared understanding" gate; distinguish facts (explore the codebase yourself) from decisions (must be made by the user) to stop self-grilling.

items.q: What should you remember about **Prototype before spec for anything front-end**?
items.a: **"raise the fidelity of the** discussion by making a cheap, rough, concrete artifact to react to".
